privacy.title: What leaves your Mac, and where it goes.
privacy.subtitle: Terminal, logs, metrics and file contents are never sent to Capstio servers. Everything the app does send out is listed below, with where it goes and when.

rows.title: SSH keys and passwords
rows.body: Stored in the macOS Keychain. Supports Secure Enclave keys and SSH agent/1Password. Keys shared with a team leave only as ciphertext in the vault.

rows.title: Terminal and commands
rows.body: Go straight from your Mac to your VPS over standard SSH, with no relay server in between.

rows.title: Logs, metrics and file contents
rows.body: Never sent to Capstio servers. Values in .env files are masked right in the editor.

rows.title: Analytics and tracking
rows.body: The app embeds no analytics or tracking SDK.

rows.title: Update checks
rows.body: The app only reads the public /appcast.xml file to compare version numbers. No identifiers or device information are sent.
rows.meta: Reads: the public /appcast.xml file · When: when the app checks for updates

rows.title: Context for AI
rows.body: Uses your own key or account, never routed through Capstio servers. Secrets are masked before sending; for full certainty, use a local model.
rows.meta: Sent to: the AI provider you choose · When: only if you turn on AI

rows.title: Team vault
rows.body: Shared hosts, SSH keys and recipes are end‑to‑end encrypted; the server stores only ciphertext. Metadata such as host count and who edited what, when, stays in plain text.
rows.meta: Sent to: Capstio servers · When: only if you sign in for team features or sync

rows.title: Slack/webhook alerts
rows.body: Alert content is sent to the address you configure.
rows.meta: Sent to: your Slack/webhook · When: only if you turn it on

rows.title: Recipe sync via Git
rows.body: Recipes you create are pushed to the Git repository you configure.
rows.meta: Sent to: your Git repository · When: only if you turn on sync

items.question: Does Capstio install anything on my VPS?
items.answer: No. Capstio connects over standard SSH and installs no agent on your VPS. Some features rely on Docker, PM2 or systemd already being on the server.

items.question: Where are my SSH keys and data stored?
items.answer: On your Mac. Passwords and private keys stay in the macOS Keychain, and terminal, logs, metrics and file contents are never sent to Capstio servers. If you use team features, the shared vault is end‑to‑end encrypted and the server stores only ciphertext.

items.question: Do I need an account?
items.answer: No. Every local feature works without one. An account is only needed for team features and sync, and you sign in with Google or a code sent by email.

items.question: Which Linux distributions are supported?
items.answer: Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 and Debian 12 come first, followed by Rocky Linux 9 and AlmaLinux 9. CentOS 7 and Alpine have limited support, and features that don't apply there are hidden.

items.question: Where can I download Capstio?
items.answer: From Capstio's GitHub Releases page, as a DMG for macOS 15 or later. Homebrew and the Mac App Store come later.
